extracted.intended_audience: New Americans (immigrants or children of immigrants) applying to graduate or professional school in the U.S. for the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Official fellowship guidance and selection criteria for the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans, describing eligibility, evaluation principles, and the qualities the program seeks in prospective fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: New American status and graduate/professional enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply for a Paul & Daisy Soros fellowship and become one of the thirty New Americans— immigrants or the children of immigrants—who are pursuing graduate or professional school in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be 'New Americans' (immigrants or children of immigrants) and pursuing graduate or professional study in the U.S.; use the eligibility quiz to confirm specifics. (Procedural timeline: application deadlines, finalist interviews, and fellowship start dates are provided.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity, originality, and initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate has demonstrated creativity, originality and initiative in one or more aspects of their life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence may come from academic work, creative achievements, leadership, projects, or other life experiences. The program emphasizes that there is no one-size-fits-all definition and looks across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to and capacity for accomplishment (drive & sustained effort)
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate has demonstrated a commitment to and capacity for accomplishment that has required drive and sustained effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for sustained achievement that reflects persistence and long-term commitment; accomplishments should be understood in the context of the applicant's opportunities and background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to constitutional values and civic principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate has demonstrated a commitment to the values expressed in the US Constitution and the Bill of Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include, but is not limited to, support of human rights and the rule of law, opposition to unwarranted encroachment on personal liberty, and advancing the responsibilities of citizenship in a free society. Examples or evidence showing civic commitment strengthen an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise of continued significant contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate has promise of continued significant contributions. Those contributions are likely to reflect distinctive creativity, originality and initiative and will mark the candidate as a leading and influential figure within their fields of endeavor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess future potential and the likelihood the applicant will become a leading/influential figure; evidence can include trajectory, ambition, prior impact, and how graduate training will enable future contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of graduate training to long-term career goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate’s graduate training is relevant to their long-term career goals and is of potential value in enhancing their future creativity and accomplishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should make clear how the proposed graduate/professional program supports their stated long-term goals and would meaningfully enhance their capacity to contribute in their field or community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic, merit-based evaluation with no preferred GPA/test-score range
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellowship program looks at applicants holistically and has never had a preferred GPA or test score range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection considers the whole application rather than numeric thresholds; the program is interested in applicants who do the most with what they have, challenge themselves, and work hard to overcome obstacles. Academic metrics are not determinative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual assessment and leveling the playing field
rubrics_metrics.description: The program seeks to create 'a level playing field' for applicants from different backgrounds, fields, stages of educational development, and ages; differences in immigration experiences are taken into account in assessing applicants’ success in meeting the selection criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate achievements relative to applicants' circumstances (including varied immigration experiences), giving weight to demonstrated accomplishment given available opportunities. This is an explicit commitment to contextualized review and equity in assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative potential to exemplify immigrant contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: We are seeking the 30 most promising New Americans who will go on to make distinctive contributions to American society, culture or their field. Each Fellow serves as an example of the richness that refugees and immigrants bring to America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who can serve as visible examples of immigrant contributions—through leadership, public engagement, or notable accomplishments—align with the fellowship’s mission. This is both an evaluative and programmatic expectation (visibility, credibility, lifelong alumni community).
